transcript: A conversation can feel less friendly, even when you don't clearly notice what's changed. In a study, people watched a group conversation and imagined being one of the speakers. Adding a four-second silence after her statement made viewers feel more rejected. Yet their estimates of the response delay didn't significantly differ from the smooth conversation group. That's the useful twist. Disrupted flow can change the feeling of connection without proving anyone dislikes you. Four seconds isn't a universal awkwardness limit, and this was a specific experimental setup. So before apologizing, separate the observation from your interpretation. Fact, they paused. Guess, they're judging me. They might be choosing their words. Give them a moment, then ask, what do you think? Treat the pause as missing information. Not a verdict.
